newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: JCI to raise Kimberley stake. [CORRECTED 05:03 GMT 5/2]
newsitem.headline: JCI to raise Kimberley stake. [CORRECTED 05:03 GMT 5/2]

text.p: (Corrects by deleting reference to Kimberley Diamond Co NL having approval from the Australian Stock Exchange for the transactions. The company now says the transactions did not require stock exchange approval and the reference was included in its announcement in error.)

Kimberley Diamond Co NL (KDC) said on Tuesday that South African-based gold producer JCI Ltd will increase its stake in the company to 37.8 percent from 11.6 percent under an asset-swap and financial agreement.

KDC said the agreement includes the consolidation of the two companies interest in Lone Star Exploration NL, which owns the Awak Mas gold project on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, as well as KDC's purchase of four JCI gold exploration projects in the Lake Victoria goldfields of Tanzania.
KDC said JCI would be able to eventually raise its stake in the company to a maximum of 51.4 percent.
KDC said it would issue up to 79.5 million shares to JCI at 35 cents each as payment for the African interests and the holding in Lone Star which would increase KDC's stake to 37.4 percent.
The company would also raise up to A$30 million from a special warrant issue in Canada at a price of 35 Australian cents per warrant, in conjunction with a 1-for-5 share consolidation.
KDC shares were one cent lower at 32 cents in late trade.
KDC said the funds received from JCI would be used for exploration programmes, as well as for possible future investments in Lone Star and for general working capital.
It said JCI could ultimately raise its holding in KDC to 51.4 percent on conversion of a A$22.5 million convertible note.
KDC chairman Miles Kennedy said the agreement would establish the company as a siginificant mining and development company which had the backing of a world-ranked gold producer.
KDC said it would be renamed Kimberley Resources Ltd.
